lacuna.name: megakernels-persistent-decode
lacuna.repo_anchor: Constraint frame (the anchor, quoted): "TU102 / sm_75 (Turing), no cp.async, no TMA, no clusters, 2-resident-CTA occupancy law, conflicted STS halves, 535 GB/s DRAM ceiling, CUDA 13.3"; workload "vLLM V1 decode step on 2x Quadro RTX 6000 (TP2, NVLink) ... W4A16 Marlin GEMMs streaming ~9 GiB/step/rank, batch 4-8, ctx 512-2048, CUDA graphs on"; owned paged-split decode-attention kernel "41.2 tok/s vs the TRITON baseline 50.1 at ctx2048; the gap is ~4.3 ms of a 24.3 ms step while attention's KV traffic is only ~0.12 ms at the DRAM wall. The residual is STRUCTURE (split-softmax workspace round-trip to DRAM, a second combine launch, step serialization), not bandwidth. Sensitivity floor learned empirically: only multi-millisecond per-step deltas move end-to-end rows." Sibling record research/decode-step-scheduling/results/gdn-step-coupling.json (2026-09-14) banks plan/0010-last-fifth #step-profile (per-kernel durations AND inter-kernel gaps ledger) and #surgeries ("graph-structure fixes") — this item feeds the same surgery set from the one-kernel-per-step literature. MEMORY.md 2026-09-08 floor: 9 GiB/card over 535 GB/s = ~57 tok/s no-MTP ceiling.
lacuna.current_status: Read 2026-09-15. The line has two poles. (1) Hand-written megakernels (Stanford Hazy Research, ThunderKittens-based): 'Look Ma, No Bubbles!' (2025-05-27) fuses the whole Llama-3.2-1B bf16 batch-1 decode into ONE persistent kernel — the paper's count of the conventional stack is ~100 kernels (7 launches/layer x 16 layers) collapsed to 1 kernel executing 7 instruction types (fused RMSNorm+QKV+RoPE; attention; ThunderGQA reduction; O-projection+residual; fused RMSNorm+up-gate+SiLU; down-projection+residual; RMSNorm+LM head) from a per-SM interpreter running a CPU-pre-generated static schedule. Measured: H100 at 78% of bandwidth, ~2.5x vLLM and >1.5x SGLang (both 'use <=50% of H100 bandwidth' on this workload); first 16-bit 1B+ forward under 1 ms on H100, <680 us on B200. Inter-kernel latency is eliminated by replacing launch boundaries with in-kernel producer-consumer: global-memory counters (completed instructions increment; dependents spin), shared-memory paging (213 kB smem = 13x16 KiB pages handed between instructions), weight prefetch across instruction boundaries, and 4-chunk consumption of the MLP input so down-projection starts before the full hidden state exists. Notably it dismisses the two launch-side shortcuts this host could imagine: PDL's cudaGridDependencySynchronize 'too coarse', CUDA graphs only cut GPU-side launch ~2.1 us -> ~1.3 us. The tensor-parallel follow-up ('We Bought the Whole GPU...' / 'How Many Llamas Can Dance in the Span of a Kernel?', 2025-09-28) takes Llama-70B 8-GPU TP to one megakernel/step with warp specialization, SMs pulling work dynamically, and in-kernel remote loads/stores replacing NCCL stream+allreduce overlap; ~22% end-to-end faster than SGLang over 65,536 ShareGPT prompts; integrated into tokasaurus, code on the Megakernels repo 'throughput' branch. The repo builds ONLY for GPU={H100,B200}. (2) Compiler line: Mirage Persistent Kernel (MPK), arXiv 2512.22219 (v1 2025-12-22, v2 2026-06-10), first compiler+runtime that mega-kernelizes multi-GPU inference via SM-level task graphs and decentralized in-kernel scheduling; up to 1.7x lower latency vs kernel-per-operator serving; code mirage-project/mirage. Ada-MK (arXiv 2605.11581, 2026) is the pre-Hopper datapoint: automated DAG-search megakernel on an NVIDIA L20 (Ada sm_89 — cp.async yes, TMA/clusters no), up to +23.6% vs TensorRT-LLM and +50.2% vs vLLM at single batch, with gains explicitly narrowing as batch grows (compute/launch tradeoff). Adjacent: FlashInfer (MLSys 2025 best paper) ships persistent decode kernels and the trtllm-gen decode path (Blackwell/PDL-centric; its GitHub README nominally claims 'SM75 (Turing) and later', but Turing support was added late and is fragile — paged prefill fails on T4 in issue #3620 (2025); issue #3675 documents a misleading 'requires sm75' error). llama.cpp is the opposite pole: stays multi-kernel, leans on op fusion + CUDA graphs by default (NVIDIA blog 2024; llama.cpp discussion #17621: 'fusing kernels reduces memory traffic and kernel launch time. Since TG is memory-bound, kernel fusion helps there the most'). llm.c runs ~one kernel per op per layer with cuDNN FlashAttention and treats launch count as a known cost.
lacuna.applicability: What transfers: the coordination model, not the artifacts. Global-memory counter synchronization + __threadfence + spinning consumers, static pre-generated schedules, chunked producer consumption, and smem page reuse are plain CUDA with no sm_90 dependency — Turing has none of TMA/clusters/mbarrier/PDL (CUDA Programming Guide sec 4.5: PDL 'available starting with devices of compute capability 9.0'), and the megakernel's own evidence says launch-side tricks (graphs: ~0.8 us/launch saved; PDL) were never where the win was anyway: the win is deleting the dependency structure that forces a full drain between walk and combine. The directly portable slice for this host is NOT a whole-model megakernel (that would mean rewriting 24 FLA-Triton GDN layers and every Marlin GEMM — months, and it attacks weight streaming, i.e. a bandwidth lever this host has falsified) but the persistent walk+combine fusion of the owned attention pair, one launch, counter-combined in-kernel. What does not transfer: ThunderKittens/H100-B200-only code (GPU= flag has no sm_75 target); batch-1 matvec economics (the 2.5x is against batch-1 stacks running <=50% of bandwidth — this host's Marlin GEMMs at batch 4-8 already stream ~9 GiB toward the 535 GB/s wall, and MEMORY.md 2026-09-08 puts the bandwidth ceiling at ~57 tok/s, i.e. the 50.1 baseline is already near the wall); Ada-MK's own narrowing-gains-at-batch finding; PDL/async-barrier machinery. CUDA 13.3 supports everything needed (cooperative-ish counter barriers are library-free).

design.mechanism: Convert the owned walk/combine pair into ONE persistent kernel. Grid: 36 SMs x 2 resident CTAs (the occupancy law, ~72 CTAs). Phase 1 (walk): each CTA loops over its (seq, head, kv-split) tiles exactly as today, keeps running (m, l, acc) in registers/smem, and at split completion writes the partial to a workspace sized to stay L2-resident on TU102 (~6 MB L2; worst case 24 heads x 8 seq x 256 dims x 4 B x n_splits <= a few MB) — this turns today's dependent DRAM round-trip into an L2 hit. Synchronization: after writing its partial, a CTA executes __threadfence() then atomicAdd(counter[seq],1) — the classic threadFenceReduction pattern; the CTA that observes counter[seq] == expected_splits becomes the combiner for that sequence, LSE-merges the siblings directly from L2 and writes final fp16 output in the row-major layout Marlin's o_proj already consumes. No second launch, no CPU-visible boundary, hence no graph-split and no drain. Counter reset must happen inside the captured graph (a tiny reset kernel node placed at graph head, or reset-by-last-reader on the previous step) or replay 2 reads stale counts. Persistent CTAs then proceed to the next layer's walk while the combiner finishes — the megakernel's cross-instruction overlap, at the scale of one op instead of one model. __nanosleep backoff on spin loops (sm_70+) to keep spinners off the 535 GB/s bus.
design.failure_modes: (a) Replay safety is the top failure: counters, not pointers, carry state between replays — a stale count either deadlocks the combiner or merges twice. Reset must be captured in-graph (see mechanism); validate with >=2 consecutive replays at fixed batch. (b) Occupancy law: if register pressure pushes the kernel below 2 CTAs/SM the counter contract still holds (it is not cooperative-launch), but the walk slows — the 41.2 tok/s kernel is already suspected occupancy-crippled, so measure CTAs/SM first. (c) Spinning on DRAM counters contends with weight streaming: gate spins behind __nanosleep and per-CTA work polling rather than tight loads. (d) Numerics: unchanged fp32 LSE math — this is a scheduling change, not a math change; outputs should be bitwise-comparable given fixed split assignment. (e) Conflicted STS halves: the combiner stages sibling partials through smem — lay out banks explicitly; do NOT reach for half2 staging tricks, this host measured half2 staging NO_DIFF in-engine. (f) Do not extend prefetch/pipelining across the KV walk — KV pipelining already measured NEGATIVE on this host; the mechanism earns from launch/dependency removal, not from more concurrency in the hot loop.
design.effort_estimate: Kernel-lane 3-5 days for the persistent walk+combine fusion (both kernels owned; most cost is in-graph counter reset wiring plus a ctx512/ctx2048 x batch4/8 sweep). The whole-model megakernel is engine-lane months and is not recommended. Gate-1 cull ~10 min: from the plan/0010 #step-profile ledger, read the walk->combine gap and combine duration; if the pair is not multi-ms the item dies cheaply.
design.priority_signal: For: aims precisely at the two named structural costs ('split-softmax workspace round-trip to DRAM, a second combine launch') and the megakernel line's 2025-2026 evidence says in-kernel counter coordination beats launch-side fixes decisively at low batch; Ada-MK proves the pattern is not Hopper-bound. Against: every measured win in the line is on bandwidth-starved batch-1 matvec stacks, which rhymes exactly with this host's falsified-bandwidth-lever lesson; the megakernel gains shrink with batch (Ada-MK), and whether walk->combine serialization is itself multi-ms at batch 4-8 under CUDA graphs is [uncertain] until the #step-profile gap ledger exists. Cull fast on that ledger.
